content.text:
I have enough to answer — shadow branches are touched by far more than rewind. Here's the full map of consumers:

**Core write path (every session, invisible to the user):**
- **Checkpoint saving** — every `SaveStep`/`SaveTaskStep` (fired by agent Stop/SubagentStop hooks) commits the working tree + transcript onto the shadow branch (`entire/<head7>-<worktree6>`). This is the main producer; rewind just reads what this wrote.
- **Condensation on `git commit`** — the prepare-commit-msg/post-commit hooks read the session's checkpoints off the shadow branch and condense them onto `entire/checkpoints/v1` (`strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go`). `content_overlap.go` also diffs against shadow-branch trees for attribution (agent-vs-human lines) at commit time.
- **Shadow branch migration** — when HEAD moves without a commit (pull/rebase/stash pop), the branch is automatically re-based onto the new base commit (`strategy/manual_commit_migration.go`); the post-rewrite hook participates after amend/rebase.
- **Orphan cleanup at session start** — a shadow branch with no matching session state file gets reset when a new session begins.

**Read paths (commands that consume shadow branch data):**
- `entire checkpoint list` / `checkpoint explain` — `explain.go:1186` searches *all* shadow branches to resolve temporary (not-yet-condensed) checkpoints by hash prefix; `ListCheckpoints` in `strategy/common.go` reads them too.
- `entire status` / session info — uncondensed step data comes from shadow-branch commits (`strategy/manual_commit_logs.go`).
- `entire doctor` — checks for ENDED sessions with uncondensed data stranded on a shadow branch and offers condense/discard repair (`doctor.go:52`).
- `entire investigate` — reads the full session transcript from the shadow branch (`investigate/loop.go`).

**Lifecycle/teardown:**
- `entire clean` (and the deprecated `reset` alias) — deletes the current HEAD's shadow branch, or all of them with the broader flag (`clean.go`, `strategy/manual_commit_reset.go`, `strategy/cleanup.go`).
- `entire disable` (`setup.go:2086`) — counts and removes all shadow branches as part of teardown.

So rewind is actually one of the smaller consumers — the load-bearing uses are checkpoint capture on every agent turn and condensation on every user commit; everything else (explain, status, doctor, investigate, clean) reads or garbage-collects what those wrote.
